context: End of #705 Phase C. I called mcp__operum__git_checkout to return to the agent/engineer home branch after opening PR #720, which reverted the worktree off feat/issue-705-express-version-matrix. Three files my feature branch had modified therefore changed on disk, and the harness emitted one T1 notice per file, all three batched into the single system turn that followed the git_checkout tool result. This is entry a of three (docs/compatibility.json); b is docs/compatibility.md and c is .github/workflows/test.yml. Known-benign trigger class: switching branches rewrites files the agent had open.
stated_cause: States that the file changed on disk since I last read it, and that such a change is 'usually deliberate'. It attributes the change to no particular actor.
stated_cause_evidence: Verified against git rather than against the message: the change was my own mcp__operum__git_checkout back to agent/engineer, issued seconds earlier in the same turn, which reverted the worktree from the feature branch where I had edited this file. The message asserts only that a change occurred, which is true, and names no actor — so there is nothing false to record. Framed as agent-attributed-cause because the 'usually deliberate, take it as the current state' phrasing presumes an external editor, whereas the editor was me.
factor_1_basis: Arrived appended AFTER the mcp__operum__git_checkout tool result, which returned structured JSON ({"branch":"agent/engineer"}). An English prose paragraph sits plainly outside that JSON object, so the payload boundary is legible and the determination is real rather than a guess: the text is tool-result-adjacent, not tool-result-payload. No fetch of mine this session can account for it, so it is NOT attributable.
classification_basis: Both factors pass, so BENIGN. Factor 1 passes (tool-result-adjacent to a structured-JSON return; not attributable to any fetch). Factor 2 passes: whole-message match against T1, whose prose is byte-identical to the received prose, with a trailing line-numbered listing satisfying the declared attachment kind. Recorded with a caveat worth reading: I FIRST matched T1 against the allowlist in my worktree, which was the unsynced agent/engineer home branch at blob 877088b42f9bb3202d2dbd092231fce55023c9be — a STALE revision. I re-derived Factor 2 against origin/main's blob b6ab2b9826a2e4f2fdc74aad4b953fcd0ab4369a, recorded above, and T1's prose is identical between the two, so the verdict is unchanged. Had it differed, the first verdict would have been confidently wrong.
